title: Best Talent Management Software in 2026: Compared by Size and Use Case
summary: We scored 12 best talent management softwares on 5 dimensions. Compare Workday, Peoplebox, Lattice, BambooHR and more by size, modules, and price for 2026.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


Most HR teams arrive here with fragmented point tools, a clunky HCM module, and succession still living in a spreadsheet. Talent management software is the layer of HR tech that runs performance reviews, goals, learning, succession, and compensation on top of your core HR system. We scored 12 platforms on the five dimensions given below so you can shortlist by fit. The right pick depends on company size:


- Enterprises land on **Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, or Oracle HCM Cloud**
- Mid-market teams land on **Lattice, HiBob, Rippling, 15Five, or Peoplebox.ai**
- Small businesses on **BambooHR** .


## Top Picks: Best Talent Management Software by Use Case


No single tool wins every situation. These are the shortlist picks by where each tool is genuinely strongest, based on module depth, verified G2 and Capterra reviews, and pricing that reflects a real deal, not a demo pitch.


- **Best for Enterprise:**Workday – deep, global HCM with talent inside a single system of record (G2 4.1/5)
- **Best for Enterprise HCM Suite (SAP-native):**SAP SuccessFactors – full talent suite for organizations already on SAP (G2 4.1/5)
- **Best for Mid-Market Talent & Performance:**Peoplebox.ai – performance and talent decisions grounded in the same goals leadership tracks (G2 4.5/5)
- **Best for Mid-Market Performance & Engagement:**Lattice – performance, engagement, and growth in one polished product (G2 4.6/5)
- **Best for Oracle-native Enterprises:**Oracle HCM Cloud – talent unified with Oracle ERP and workforce planning (G2 3.8/5)
- **Best for HR + IT + Finance unified:**Rippling – the only HRIS offering native IT and finance integration (G2 4.8/5)
- **Best for Modern Mid-Market HRIS:**HiBob – skills-based framework with fast global adoption (G2 4.5/5)
- **Best for Small Business:**BambooHR – HR basics plus lightweight talent tools that teams adopt fast (G2 4.4/5)
- **Best for Manager-led Performance:**15Five – coaching-first performance for manager-heavy scale-ups (G2 4.6/5)
- **Best for Learning:**Cornerstone OnDemand – the widest LMS and skills library in the category (G2 4.1/5)
- **Best for Global Teams:**Dayforce – payroll-led HCM with talent modules across 160+ countries (G2 4.2/5)
- **Best for Engagement-Led Talent:**Culture Amp – engagement data feeding performance and development (G2 4.5/5)


How We Picked (Methodology of choosing the top tools)


We started with 45 talent platforms named across G2 grids, Capterra listings, and analyst shortlists. We shortlisted 12 that ship the core talent modules and have at least 100 verified G2 reviews. Every shortlisted tool was then pressure-tested against feedback we collected from HR leaders and practitioners in the Peoplebox customer network. **No vendor paid to be included, and no vendor previewed this page.**


Each tool was scored on five dimensions: **module fit, HRIS and payroll integration, manager and employee adoption, talent analytics and reporting, and total cost including implementation** . The full decision framework, with the exact question to ask each vendor, is in theHow to Choose section below.


Where a claim needs benchmark evidence, we draw from Peoplebox’s proprietary[2026 State of Performance Management Report](https://www.peoplebox.ai/analyticslab/2026-performance-management-statistics-report/) , which surveys HR leaders on review cadence, calibration practice, and adoption benchmarks that vendor marketing rarely publishes.


Ratings come from G2 and Capterra, with the pull date next to each score. Pricing is what the vendor lists publicly or confirms in a demo; where a vendor only quotes on request, we say so.


## What Is Talent Management Software?


Talent management software is the layer of HR tech that runs performance reviews, goals, learning, succession, and compensation on top of your core HR system. It turns headcount data into talent decisions: who is ready for promotion, where the flight risk sits, and which teams need coaching.


The category is used loosely. “Software,” “system,” and “platform” are used interchangeably by vendors and mean the same thing. It is not an HCM or HRIS, an ATS, or a talent relationship management software. The table below shows how each of these differs from a talent management system.


For the discipline itself (talent strategy, frameworks, and processes), see the[talent management framework guide](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/talent-management-framework/) . This page is about the software that runs it.


Category What it is Why it is not this page


HCM / HRIS The broader system of record for core HR, payroll, benefits, and time. Talent management is the layer that sits on top of HCM and HRIS to develop and retain people.


ATS (Applicant Tracking System) A recruiting tool that tracks applicants through the hiring pipeline before they are hired. Talent management covers the post-hire lifecycle: performance, goals, learning, succession, and compensation.


Talent relationship management software A candidate CRM for building talent pipelines and nurturing leads before they apply. A recruiting product, separate from the post-hire talent lifecycle this guide covers.


What a Talent Management System Includes


A modern talent management system bundles seven to eight core modules. Few tools do all of them well, which is why the right pick depends on which modules matter most to your team.


1. **Performance management & reviews** : check-ins, appraisals, and calibration; the module HR uses most.
2. **Goals and OKRs** : cascade objectives from company to team to person and track progress in-flow.
3. **Learning & development** : course delivery, skills tracking, and manager-assigned paths.
4. **Succession planning** : nine-box grids, readiness maps, and internal mobility pipelines.
5. **Compensation management** : merit cycles, budget modeling, and pay equity checks.
6. **Engagement surveys** : pulse and annual surveys with manager-level heatmaps.
7. **Talent analytics & reporting** : the layer that turns all of the above into decisions.
8. **Recruiting & onboarding** : bundled into fuller suites but often bought separately.

The 12 Best Talent Management Software Platforms


Each profile below uses the same template: what the tool is, how it scores across the five dimensions, what stands out, where it is not the fit, and a plain verdict. Segments are ordered by size, not by preference. If you want to compare these vendors against the Peoplebox.ai platform, see[Peoplebox talent management software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/talent-management-software/) .


1. Workday – Enterprise HCM suite


Best For


Fortune 500 and 1,000+ employee enterprises needing end-to-end talent management.


**Rating:**[G2 4.1/5](https://www.g2.com/products/workday-hcm/reviews) (1,713 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.5/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/66908/Workday-HCM/#reviews) (1,772 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** Contact sales (premium pricing per reviewer)


**What it is:** Workday is an enterprise-grade talent management suite that positions itself as “human potential, elevated by AI.” It covers recruiting, onboarding, performance, learning, and mobility inside one unified platform and is used by many Fortune 500 organizations, replacing legacy HCM.


- **Module fit:** Talent Acquisition, AI for Recruiting, Onboarding, Talent Optimization, AI Talent Mobility, Learning Management, and Talent Management Agent.
- **Integration:** Unified natively with Workday Finance and Planning; partner integrations are extensive but often need enterprise services to wire.
- **Adoption:** G2 reviewers consistently flag heavy click depth, a steep learning curve for new admins, and complex menu systems.
- **Analytics:** Best-in-class enterprise workforce analytics powered by a large proprietary dataset.
- **Cost and implementation:** Premium pricing (not disclosed publicly). Reviewers describe it as expensive for smaller businesses, with sluggish performance during peak hours.


**What stands out:** Leader in the[2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant](https://www.gartner.com/doc/reprints?id=00ThR00000DFKgZUAX&ct=260831&st=sb) for Talent Acquisition Suites, and one platform for HR, payroll, finance, and talent at global scale.


**Where it is not the fit:** Overkill and slow to configure for organizations under a few thousand employees; reviewers cite cumbersome reporting and limited customization in some areas.


**Verdict:** Shortlist if you are enterprise-scale and replacing your HCM. Skip if you are mid-market and want fast time-to-value.


2. SAP SuccessFactors – SAP-native talent suite


Best For


Global organizations, particularly SAP-native shops, needing recruiting-through-offboarding coverage.


**Rating:**[G2 4.1/5](https://www.g2.com/products/sap-sap-successfactors-hcm/reviews) (1,656 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.0/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/144575/SuccessFactors-Perform-and-Reward/#reviews) (294 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** Contact sales (higher than competitors per reviewers)


**What it is:** SAP SuccessFactors is an AI-driven talent management suite anchored by SAP’s Talent Intelligence Hub. It runs recruiting, performance and goals, compensation, learning, leadership development, and succession for large multinationals already standardized on the SAP stack.


- **Module fit:** Recruiting and onboarding, performance and goals, compensation, continuous learning, leadership and talent development, and succession planning.
- **Integration:** Strong native integration with the rest of SAP; standard connectors to non-SAP HRIS and payroll systems.
- **Adoption:** Steep learning curve requiring extensive training; outdated UI reviewers describe as clunky; inconsistent experience across modules; poor mobile responsiveness.
- **Analytics:** Strong once configured; reporting typically requires SAP-specific expertise.
- **Cost and implementation:** Not disclosed publicly; reviewers note higher price versus competitors and significant implementation costs.


**What stands out:** Named[IDC, 2025](https://my.idc.com/getdoc.jsp?containerId=US52995425) with an AI-driven talent intelligence hub that unifies employee skills, career data, and learning.


**Where it is not the fit:** Not a fit for mid-market or SMB. Expensive implementation and licensing for smaller organizations, and configuration flexibility is a repeated pain point for teams outside SAP-heavy environments.


**Verdict:** Shortlist if you already run SAP. Otherwise, the switching cost is difficult to justify.


3. Peoplebox.ai – AI talent management platform


Best For


Mid-market companies (50 to 2,000 employees) wanting OKR-driven AI talent management with native Slack and Microsoft Teams experience.


**Rating:**[G2 4.5/5](https://www.g2.com/products/peoplebox-ai/reviews) (369 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.6/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/197968/Peoplebox/) (244 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** From $8/user/mo (Talent Mgmt)


**What it is:** Peoplebox.ai is a dynamic performance, OKR, talent management, and people analytics platform designed to help companies align and retain top performers. It brings company and individual goals, performance, and talent decisions into a single system that syncs with 50+ work tools in real time. globally.


- **Module fit:** Performance reviews, OKRs and goal management, 1:1 meetings, employee pulse surveys, 360-degree feedback, dynamic org chart, HR analytics (50+ parameters), calibration, and compensation planning.
- **Integration:** 50+ work tools including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Sheets, Jira, plus HRIS, payroll, and performance systems with real-time sync.
- **Adoption:** Deep Slack and Microsoft Teams integration means reviews and check-ins happen in-flow, without another tool to open. Capterra reviewers flag navigation complexity in some sub-fields.
- **Analytics:** HR analytics across 50+ parameters; automated calibration replaces spreadsheet-driven review cycles.
- **Cost and implementation:** Talent Management $8/user/month (OKRs/ Goals + Performance Reviews + Continuous Feedback). Typical rollout in 2 to 4 weeks.


**What stands out:** One platform for OKRs, performance, and analytics with a native Slack and Teams experience, phase-wise cycle management, mid-cycle adjustments, and automated calibration.


**Where it is not the fit:** No mobile app (G2 reviewers); some UI latency while toggling screens as per capterra reviewer.


**Verdict:** Shortlist if you want OKR-driven performance and talent inside Slack or Teams. Look elsewhere if you need a full HCM system of record with payroll.

4. Oracle HCM Cloud – Oracle-native HCM suite


Best For


1,000+ employee enterprises standardized on Oracle wanting a single source of truth for people, work, and skills.


**Rating:**[G2 3.8/5](https://www.g2.com/products/oracle-talent-management-cloud-formerly-taleo/reviews) (89 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.0/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/72011/Oracle-HCM-Cloud/#reviews) (92 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** Contact sales (top-tier pricing per reviewers; ~10-month implementation)


**What it is:** Oracle Talent Management is a unified, AI-embedded cloud solution powered by a single talent profile that connects people, work, and skills data with intelligent agentic apps. It fits organizations already running Oracle Fusion / HCM.


- **Module fit:** Recruiting, performance management, compensation, learning, and succession planning; unified with all Fusion / HCM modules.
- **Integration:** Native to Oracle Fusion / HCM; connectors to Skillsoft, LinkedIn Learning, Coursera, Slack, and Microsoft Teams; APIs and file-based exchange.
- **Adoption:** Reviewers note slow performance with large data loads, complex navigation, a non-intuitive interface, and multiple steps for common processes.
- **Analytics:** Deep once configured; requires Oracle expertise to fully unlock.
- **Cost and implementation:** Perceived as a top-tier cost with a typical 10-month implementation timeline noted by reviewers.


**What stands out:** Thousands of new capabilities delivered each quarter and AI-embedded across the suite with agentic apps.


**Where it is not the fit:** G2 scores trail Oracle’s direct competitors (SAP 4.1, ServiceNow 4.3, Darwinbox 4.4). Not a fit for organizations wanting time-to-value in months, or non-Oracle stacks.


**Verdict:** Shortlist if you are Oracle-native. Skip otherwise.


5. Dayforce – Global payroll-led HCM


Best For


Mid-market to enterprise (100 to 12,000+ employees) in retail, hospitality, manufacturing, and financial services.


**Rating:**[G2 4.2/5](https://www.g2.com/products/dayforce/reviews?source=search) (961 reviews)·[Capterra 4.3/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/198964/Dayforce-Powerpay/#reviews) (1,063 reviews, Sep 2026)· **Starting price:** Contact sales


**What it is:** Dayforce is a talent management suite that supports the full employee lifecycle from hire to retire, layered onto a native payroll and workforce management engine. It is and is strongest in shift-worker and frontline-heavy industries.


- **Module fit:** Recruiting, onboarding, performance management, engagement, compensation, learning, succession planning, and Career Explorer for internal mobility.
- **Integration:** Native payroll and workforce management; integrations to other HR systems not detailed on the product page.
- **Adoption:** G2 reviewers flag a steep learning curve and complex navigation, slow customer support response times, and occasional app freezes.
- **Analytics:** Strong on labor cost, workforce planning, and compliance reporting for frontline industries.
- **Cost and implementation:** Not disclosed publicly. Frequent system updates require re-learning; reporting creation from scratch is unintuitive.


**What stands out:** Full employee lifecycle inside one payroll-native platform, with a Career Explorer feature that drives internal mobility.


**Where it is not the fit:** Some features lack modern AI capabilities compared with newer entrants. Not the best pick when the primary need is a specialist performance or engagement product.


**Verdict:** Shortlist for global enterprises replacing legacy payroll plus talent together, especially in retail, hospitality, or manufacturing.


6. Cornerstone OnDemand – Enterprise LMS + talent


Best For


Enterprise and SMB organizations that want learning, performance, mobility, and succession connected in one data model.


**Rating:**[G2 4.0/5](https://www.g2.com/sellers/cornerstone-ondemand#reviews) (530 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.3/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/148621/Cornerstone-Performance/#reviews) (232 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** Package-based (Elevate+, Intelligence+); contact sales


**What it is:** Cornerstone connects learning, performance, mobility, and succession in a single data model so managers coach better and employees grow. Known as the enterprise LMS standard.


- **Module fit:** Performance management, internal mobility/talent marketplace, succession planning, recruiting and onboarding, AI Performance / Goal / Succession assistants, AI-generated development plans, and enterprise LMS.
- **Integration:** Salesforce, Microsoft Teams, Workday, other HR and CRM systems, ATS, and payroll software.
- **Adoption:** G2 reviewers describe a clunky UX with an outdated interface, a steep learning curve requiring expert configuration, and slow customer support.
- **Analytics:** Strong on learning analytics and skills reporting; talent analytics rated average.
- **Cost and implementation:** Package-based plans (Elevate+, Intelligence+); no specific price disclosed. Integration issues with licensed content and complicated permission structures are cited.


**What stands out:** Most talent tools ship learning, performance, and succession as separate modules; Cornerstone connects them in one data model.


**Where it is not the fit:** Mobile app lags behind desktop; if the primary need is performance or OKRs, Cornerstone is overkill.


**Verdict:** Shortlist if learning is your #1 module. Skip if you only need reviews and goals.


7. BambooHR – SMB HR + light talent


Best For


Small to mid-sized businesses (typically 51 to 200 employees) wanting one easy-to-use HR platform.


**Rating:**[G2 4.4/5](https://www.g2.com/sellers/bamboohr#reviews) (6,736 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.6/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/110968/BambooHR/#reviews) (3,557 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** Contact sales (per-employee tiered; add-ons inflate cost)


**What it is:** BambooHR is the complete HR platform for small business, covering people records, onboarding, performance, engagement, payroll, and benefits under one interface. It is the default HR system for US small and mid-sized businesses that want HR basics plus light talent tools without an enterprise rollout.


- **Module fit:** Applicant tracking, candidate experience, onboarding, performance growth, recognition and awards, employee records, automated reporting, time tracking, benefits enrollment, payroll automation, compensation planning, and benchmarking data.
- **Integration:** Broad pre-built integrations across the HR stack.
- **Adoption:** Top-rated for ease of use across G2 and Capterra. Even one-person HR departments can run it, per the vendor.
- **Analytics:** Standard reporting suite; add-ons available for advanced needs.
- **Cost and implementation:** Different plans. Core $10/employee/mo, Pro $17/employee/mo, Elite $17/employee/mo. Reviewers note it becomes pricey with add-ons.


**What stands out:** The default HR platform for small business, combining core HR records, onboarding, performance, engagement, and payroll under one interface that non-HR managers can pick up without training.


**Where it is not the fit:** Limited enterprise-level customization, integration challenges with third-party tools, and scalability constraints at enterprise headcount. International payroll gets complex.


**Verdict:** Shortlist under 200 employees. Layer a dedicated performance tool on top as you scale past mid-market.


8. Rippling – Unified HR, IT & finance


Best For


Fast-scaling SMBs (50 to 500 employees) and enterprises wanting HR, IT, and finance unified in one platform.


**Rating:**[G2 4.8/5](https://www.g2.com/sellers/rippling#reviews) (13,412 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.9/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/172127/Rippling/#reviews) (4,872 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** Contact Sales


**What it is:** Rippling is a single source of truth combining recruiting and HR data with native IT and finance integration. It puts HR busywork on autopilot and is rated G2 #1 HCM Software.


- **Module fit:** Employee records (Employee Graph), onboarding/offboarding, time and attendance, performance management, compliance, recruiting, IT management, and finance.
- **Integration:** 650+ third-party app integrations including LinkedIn, Indeed, Greenhouse, Lever, Google Workspace, Slack, and Zoom.
- **Adoption:** Steep initial learning curve due to extensive feature surface; setup and configuration are time-consuming.
- **Analytics:** Cross-system reporting across HR, IT, and finance is a repeated strength.
- **Cost and implementation:** No specific price disclosed on their website.


**What stands out:** Only HRIS offering native IT and finance integration; advanced workflow automation with 100+ templates. Rated G2 #1 HCM Software with 9.3/10 G2 support.


**Where it is not the fit:** Limited customization for certain workflows and reporting; performance slowness with large datasets; add-on modules inflate costs. Some features are not available in every region.


**Verdict:** Shortlist when you are consolidating HR, IT, and finance together and want automation baked in.


9. HiBob – Modern mid-market HRIS


Best For


Modern, fast-growing, global mid-market businesses wanting an integrated, skills-based talent suite.


**Rating:**[G2 4.5/5](https://www.g2.com/sellers/hibob#reviews) (2,636 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.6/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/156106/Hibob/#reviews) (179 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** Contact sales (higher-priced per reviewers)


**What it is:** HiBob’s Bob is a Talent Suite that connects hiring, performance management, and learning through a unified skills-based framework. It is designed for the AI era with an intuitive interface that drives fast adoption.


- **Module fit:** Bob Hiring (structured workflows, 2,000+ job boards, AI CV matching), Bob Talent (performance reviews, goals, 1-on-1s, feedback), Bob Learning (programs, personalized journeys, AI course creation), and Bob Skills (unified taxonomy).
- **Integration:** Zoom, LinkedIn, Slack, Udemy, Go1, Google Calendar, Canditech, Microsoft Outlook, and Greenhouse.
- **Adoption:** Designed for fast adoption; managers and employees pick it up quickly on the modern UX. The mobile app is limited compared to desktop.
- **Analytics:** Skills-based analytics and people insights across hiring, performance, and learning.
- **Cost and implementation:** Not publicly disclosed; reviewers note higher pricing relative to competitors.


**What stands out:** Skills-based framework that connects hiring, performance, and learning; GDPR, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliant with AI-powered CV matching, scorecards, and course creation.


**Where it is not the fit:** Performance management features need improvement per Capterra reviewers; slow report loading; limited customization for complex org structures and limited recruitment / ATS integration.


**Verdict:** Shortlist for global mid-market companies that want HRIS plus talent together on a skills-based backbone.


10. Lattice – Performance and engagement platform


Best For


SMB to enterprise organizations seeking integrated performance reviews, goals, 1:1s, and feedback in one system.


**Rating:**[G2 4.6/5](https://www.g2.com/sellers/lattice#reviews) (4,124 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.5/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/151676/Lattice/#reviews) (207 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** From $13/seat/mo (Foundations); modules from $4 to $10; min $4k/yr


**What it is:** Lattice is a mid-market performance product covering reviews, goals and OKRs, 1:1s, engagement, compensation, and growth. It is popular with tech and services companies in the 200 to 2,000 employee band that want performance and engagement in one platform rather than stitched-together point tools.


- **Module fit:** Performance reviews (AI-drafted), talent reviews, PIPs, succession planning, 1:1s, weekly updates, feedback, Q&A boards, goals and OKRs, engagement surveys, compensation, and Grow (development).
- **Integration:** Deep Workday integration highlighted; Slack, Jira, Salesforce, and mainstream HRIS.
- **Adoption:** Steep learning curve for new users; cluttered interface in certain areas; missing group 1:1 functionality.
- **Analytics:** AI-drafted reviews grounded in Lattice data; reporting customization is limited per reviewer.
- **Cost and implementation:** Foundations $13/seat/mo (most popular); Performance $10; Goals & OKRs $8; Engagement $4; add-ons: Compensation +$6, Grow +$4. Minimum $4,000/year.


**What stands out:** A polished performance product where reviews, goals, 1:1s, and growth plans read as one integrated flow rather than bolted-on modules, with AI-drafted review copy that draws from the same feedback and goal data managers use every week.


**Where it is not the fit:** Limited customization for reviews and workflows, complex initial setup, and high pricing relative to features per reviewer.


**Verdict:** Shortlist if performance and engagement are the primary needs. Compare against Peoplebox if OKRs are central to how leadership tracks work.


11. Culture Amp – Engagement-led talent suite


Best For


Mid-market to enterprise organizations focused on engagement-led development (professional services, financial services, software, manufacturing).


**Rating:**[G2 4.5/5](https://www.g2.com/search?query=Culture+Amp) (1,614 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.6/5](https://www.capterra.com/search/?query=Culture+Amp) (163 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** Contact sales


**What it is:** Culture Amp is an engagement-first talent product built around science-backed survey templates and career development, positioned to drive engagement, performance, and retention at scale.


- **Module fit:** Career paths and competencies, personalized growth plans, develop analytics, continuous feedback, performance reviews, 1-on-1 conversations, goal management, engagement surveys, and AI Coach.
- **Integration:** HRIS integrations mentioned generally; specific integration list not detailed on the landing page.
- **Adoption:** Limited customization and difficult navigation cited in G2 and Capterra reviews. Performance module feels clunky and disconnected from the survey module, per reviewers.
- **Analytics:** Strong benchmarking with a large global engagement dataset; powerful AI for data analysis and comment summarization.
- **Cost and implementation:** Not publicly disclosed; reviewers describe high pricing relative to features.


**What stands out:** An engagement-led product that pairs survey templates with an AI Coach that summarizes comment themes so managers can act on employee feedback without reading every response.


**Where it is not the fit:** Performance management features are less developed than the survey module, and scaling can be limited for larger enterprises.


**Verdict:** Shortlist when engagement is the leading talent signal you optimize around; look elsewhere for a full performance system.


12. 15Five – Manager-led performance platform


Best For


Mid-market organizations (100 to 1,000+ employees) focused on manager enablement and continuous performance management.


**Rating:**[G2 4.6/5](https://www.g2.com/search?query=15Five) (1,927 reviews) ·[Capterra 4.7/5](https://www.capterra.com/search/?query=15Five) (895 reviews, Sep 2026) · **Starting price:** Tiered (Engage / Perform / Total / Transform); pricing on request


**What it is:** 15Five is an AI-powered employee performance management and engagement platform built to help HR leaders and managers improve performance, increase engagement, and reduce turnover.


- **Module fit:** Perform (reviews, check-ins, 1-on-1 agendas, feedback, recognition, AI-assisted reviews), Compensation (insights, pay ranges, benchmarking, total rewards), Engage (predictive analytics, surveys, action planning), Growth Studio (9-box, IDPs, PIPs, succession), plus AMAYA AI and Kona AI Assistant.
- **Integration:** HRIS connector with automatic user sync, SSO tools, Slack, BambooHR, and ADP.
- **Adoption:** Steep learning curve with many features enabled by default; navigation challenges for analytics and reporting; mobile app requires too many clicks per reviewer.
- **Analytics:** Predictive engagement analytics and manager-effectiveness insights; AMAYA AI agent for people insights.
- **Cost and implementation:** Multiple tiers (Engage, Perform, Total Platform, Transform). Reviewers describe cost as higher than market value with limited contract flexibility.


**What stands out:** Unifies performance, engagement, and retention through manager effectiveness with AI assistants baked in.


**Where it is not the fit:** Limited customization for templates and surveys; complex setup without proper onboarding; high price relative to market per reviewers.


**Verdict:** Shortlist for manager-heavy orgs that want continuous performance plus engagement in a weekly rhythm.


## How to Choose Talent Management Software (5 Evaluation Dimensions)


Every vendor sells the same broad promise. The five questions below are how you separate them on your actual buying criteria. Ask each vendor to answer them in a live demo, not on a call. For the discipline behind the buying framework, see the[talent management framework guide](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/talent-management-framework/) .


1. **Module fit:** Does the system go deep on the modules you need, or is talent a checkbox in a bigger suite?
2. **HRIS and payroll integration:** Does it connect to your system of record, or does it create another silo?
3. **Manager and employee adoption:** Will managers open it every week, or will it join the graveyard of HR tools nobody uses?
4. **Talent analytics and reporting:** Can you answer “who is ready for the next role” and “where is the flight risk” without pulling a spreadsheet?
5. **Total cost including implementation:** What is the real one-year price once you add setup, training, and internal effort?

## How Much Does Talent Management Software Cost?


Talent management software is priced in three ways, and the range you pay is set more by your headcount and modules than by the vendor you pick.


- **Per-employee-per-month (PEPM):** $4 to $15 per user per month is the mid-market band. Includes Lattice, 15Five, Peoplebox.ai.
- **Module-based:** Vendors like BambooHR and Culture Amp sell talent as bundled add-ons to core HR or engagement, priced per module.
- **Enterprise “contact sales”:** Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle, Cornerstone, and Dayforce quote based on headcount, modules, and services.


**What drives the real price:** Integrations to your HRIS or payroll can add setup fees, and per-module upsells (learning, comp, surveys) are common on suites.


**Is there free talent management software?** A handful of tools have free tiers (Effy AI for 360s, Zoho People at low cost, open-source HRIS like OrangeHRM with talent add-ons). Talent Management and Succession Planning


Succession planning is the module that separates a real talent suite from a performance review tool. A serious system maps readiness, tracks internal mobility, and gives leadership a nine-box view they can act on in one place.


How the shortlist handles succession:


- **Deep succession modules:** Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Cornerstone, Oracle HCM, and Dayforce. These support nine-box grids, readiness scoring, career pathing, and skills gap analysis at enterprise scale.
- **Mid-market succession:** Peoplebox.ai, Lattice, and HiBob offer succession views built on performance and OKR data, without the enterprise configuration overhead.
- **Light or missing:** Most SMB and engagement-first tools (BambooHR, Culture Amp, 15Five) do not run true succession planning. Teams under 200 typically manage this in a spreadsheet.


If succession is a primary buying criterion, focus your shortlist on enterprise suites or mid-market platforms that ship succession as a first-class module, not an afterthought.


Implementing Talent Management Software


Time-to-value depends on segment and vendor. A specialist tool can be live in weeks. An enterprise HCM suite is a multi-quarter project. Plan for both the technical rollout and the culture change that makes managers use the tool.


1. **Weeks 1 to 2 – Foundations:** Pick a sponsor, map integrations to your HRIS or payroll, and finalize the review cycle you want to run.
2. **Weeks 3 to 4 – Configure:** Load users and orgs, set up review templates, configure OKR structure, and connect Slack or Teams.
3. **Weeks 5 to 6 – Manager enablement:** Train managers first; they are the adoption bottleneck.
4. **Weeks 7 to 8 – Launch and iterate:** Run the first cycle with a small cohort, gather feedback, then expand company-wide.


**Why talent initiatives fail:** Reasons are weak manager training, poor HRIS integration that forces duplicate data entry, and no[clear owner after launch](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/what-is-talent-retention/) . Every one of these is a rollout problem, not a product problem.

## FAQs


### What is talent management software?


### What is the difference between talent management software and an HCM or HRIS?


HCM/HRIS is the broader system of record for core HR, payroll, and benefits. Talent management is the layer on top: performance, goals, learning, succession, and compensation. Most mid-market teams run an HRIS plus a dedicated talent platform; enterprises often buy both from one HCM suite.


### What are the best talent management tools?


The strongest picks in 2026 are Workday and SAP SuccessFactors for enterprise, Peoplebox and Lattice for mid-market performance and OKRs, BambooHR for small business, Dayforce for global teams, and Cornerstone for enterprise learning. The right choice depends on modules, size, and budget.


### How much does a talent management system cost?


Mid-market per-user pricing runs $4 to $15 per user per month. Enterprise HCM suites like Workday start in the six figures per year. Implementation and services often add 20 to 40 percent in year one, and integrations to your HRIS or payroll can add setup fees.


### Is there free talent management software?


A few tools offer free tiers: Effy AI for 360 feedback, Zoho People at low cost, and open-source HRIS like OrangeHRM with talent add-ons. Free rarely scales past 25 users and none replace a paid platform for a mid-market team running reviews, OKRs, and analytics together.


### What is the best talent management software for small business?


Under 200 employees, BambooHR is the strongest pick. It deploys in days, costs around $6 per user per month, and covers HR basics with light performance and engagement modules. Layer a dedicated performance tool on top as you scale past 200.


### What is the best talent management software for large companies?


At 2,000+ employees, Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM Cloud, and Dayforce lead. They offer full HCM with deep succession, comp, and workforce planning. Expect six-figure annual pricing and 9 to 18 month implementations, and plan for adoption programs on top.


### What features should talent management software include?


A modern platform bundles performance reviews, goals or OKRs, learning and development, succession planning, compensation, engagement surveys, and talent analytics. Fuller suites also cover recruiting and onboarding. Few tools do all of them well, so shortlist by the modules that matter most.


### Does talent management software include succession planning?


Enterprise suites like Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Cornerstone, Oracle, and Dayforce ship deep succession planning with nine-box grids and readiness maps. Mid-market platforms like Peoplebox, Lattice, and HiBob offer lighter succession views built on performance data. Most SMB tools do not run true succession planning.


### Which HCM tool is best?


It depends on size and stack. Workday is the enterprise default; SAP SuccessFactors fits SAP shops; Oracle HCM suits Oracle-native orgs; Dayforce anchors payroll-first buyers; BambooHR and HiBob anchor SMB and mid-market. Match the tool to your existing systems and headcount.


### How is talent management software different from talent relationship management software?


Talent relationship management (TRM) is a recruiting tool for building candidate pipelines and nurturing leads before they apply. Talent management software runs the post-hire lifecycle: reviews, goals, learning, succession, and comp. They solve different problems and are typically bought separately.


### How long does it take to implement talent management software?


A specialist mid-market platform can be live in two to eight weeks. Bundled HR and talent suites take four to ten weeks. Enterprise HCM implementations run six to eighteen months. Manager training and HRIS integration are the two levers that determine whether the rollout sticks.
